name: Chunk-based spatial partitioning
text:
# Chunk-based spatial partitioning


## Overview
Chunk-based spatial partitioning decomposes a volumetric dataset into fixed-size, non-overlapping spatial subvolumes (chunks) to enable efficient memory management, parallel processing, and out-of-core streaming. It differs from hierarchical methods like [Chunk Trees](4050-chunk-trees.md) by using a flat or [uniform grid](#920-uniform-grid.md) structure, and from distributed approaches like [MPI-based Volume Partitioning](1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md) by focusing on the fundamental unit of data locality and lifecycle management rather than just network distribution.

## Shared principles
The method relies on dividing the global domain $\Omega$ into a set of chunks $C_i$. For a [regular grid](#3950-regular-grid.md), the chunk index $\mathbf{k} = (k_x, k_y, k_z)$ for a voxel at global coordinate $\mathbf{p} = (x, y, z)$ is calculated as:
$$
k_x = \lfloor x / W_x \rfloor, \quad k_y = \lfloor y / W_y \rfloor, \quad k_z = \lfloor z / W_z \rfloor
$$
where $W_x, W_y, W_z$ are the chunk dimensions in voxels [Parent]. This allows $O(1)$ determination of the chunk containing any sample point.

To mitigate boundary artifacts (e.g., black stripes in [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) or discontinuities in [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md)) caused by rendering kernels spanning chunk edges, an overlap region of width $w_{overlap}$ is often included. Data from adjacent chunks is loaded into the overlap region but masked out during final compositing or stitching [Parent].

## Subtopics

### [MPI-based Volume Partitioning](1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md)
A [data-parallel](#6292-slice-parallelisation.md) strategy that decomposes a volume into contiguous slices along one axis and assigns each to an MPI process. It minimizes inter-process communication during computation, relying on post-processing assembly. Choose this for static, large-scale distributed rendering.

### [Chunk-based World Streaming](2369-chunk-based-world-streaming.md)
Manages chunk lifecycle, I/O scheduling, and state transitions (generation, meshing, unloading) based on player position. Choose this for dynamic, cache-aware loading in interactive applications like voxel games.

### [Chunk-based Training](3168-chunk-based-training.md)
Partitions the global volume into chunks to enable parallel neural network optimization across multiple GPUs. It scales coordinate spaces (e.g., $[-0.5, 0.5]^3$ for 8 chunks) to fit single-GPU memory. Choose this for training large implicit [neural volume](#912-neural-volumes.md) representations.

### [Chunk Trees](4050-chunk-trees.md)
A planet-wide octree-based method that organizes data into hierarchical [chunk trees](#4050-chunk-trees.md) to eliminate visible refinement artifacts. It enforces a screen-space cut covering the entire world to prevent checker-hole artifacts. Choose this for seamless, high-fidelity terrain rendering from ground to orbit.

### [Object-space decomposition with local clustering](4156-object-space-decomposition-with-local-clustering.md)
Partitions unstructured volumes into geometrically connected cell-clusters using [graph partitioning](#4250-remapping-phase.md) (MeTiS). It minimizes boundary faces and load imbalance. Choose this for parallel [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) of unstructured grids.

### [Uniform Block Partitioning with Acceleration](6098-uniform-block-partitioning-with-acceleration.md)
Subdivides volumes into uniform blocks and applies [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) techniques like [empty space skipping](#1002-empty-space-skipping.md) and early ray termination. Choose this for single-node interactive rendering optimization.

### [Moving Walls Algorithm](9715-moving-walls-algorithm.md)
Partitions data into cells containing closely cropped blocks of data, optimized for target memory size and viewpoint using a kd-tree. Choose this for view-dependent, memory-constrained streaming.

### VOGUE Parallel Operation
A hardware-specific parallel operation where the dataset is divided into subvolumes distributed across processing units. Each unit processes a ray while it traverses its subvolume, sending ray properties to neighboring units on exit [S1].
*   **Communication:** Uses a multi-master bus for up to 8 engines (640MB/s bandwidth) or a ring-connected cubic network for larger setups (e.g., 4x4x4 units), requiring ~27MB/s per link and ~5.2GB/s total [S1].
*   **Pitfall:** Gaps between subvolumes must be removed to avoid visual artifacts by replicating boundary voxels [S1].

### Efficient Query on Standard PCs
An efficient data querying technique for large multivariate volume datasets, based on precomputed per-block Gaussian mixture models and run-time ellipse-polygon [intersection detection](#1705-voxel-filled-check.md) [S2, unofficial].
*   **Steps:** Precompute Gaussian mixture models per block, then perform run-time ellipse-polygon intersection detection for data value querying [S2, unofficial].
*   **Comparison:** Unlike hierarchical acceleration techniques like octrees, which may not be beneficial for very dense multivariate data, this method uses precomputed models for efficient querying [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of partitioning volumes into chunks for parallel processing dates back to early hardware architectures. The [VOGUE](#3149-vogue-architecture.md) system (1995) implemented a parallel architecture where datasets were divided into subvolumes distributed across different units, with ray properties passed between neighboring units [S1]. This approach required specific data distribution schemes to remove gaps between subvolumes by replicating boundary voxels [S1].
